name: Promenade Chassé
notes: Owner's description (2026-11-16): the chassé after the Whisk, travelling in promenade, with a full lift onto the toes as the feet come together on the half beat; the couple stays in promenade and turns to face in the next figure (an Open Natural Turn). Named after the American-style Promenade Chassé, which stays in promenade; the International Chassé from Promenade Position has the follow turn to face during the chassé instead. Timing 1, 2 & 3. Starts in crossed promenade and travels towards the open side of the V: diagonally forward left for the lead (facing 315), diagonally forward right for the follow (facing 225), so due -x in the figure's frame. Count 1: the lead's right foot forward and across, 0.25 m (reduced from 0.5 m for the 2026-11-18 repair). Count 2: the crossed foot comes from behind to the original landing point, using a shallow outward arc with departure -65 degrees for lead / +65 degrees for follow, so it clears the standing footprint. The original 0.85 forward / 0.75 across offsets are retained. Both pelvises remain 0.06 m behind their weighted support along the line of travel during this side step, returning to zero on the close; this represents collection over the feet without the previous deep crouch. &: close to 0.1 apart (narrower than the usual 0.2, so the partners' inner feet stay well clear of each other), taking weight late. Count 3: 0.4 along the line again. The original sizes matched the other waltz figures (0.5 first step, side steps 0.4); this repair shortens only the first step to 0.25. Rise: 'a full lift onto toes' written as 0.1 (the model only has a height), 0.06 by the end of 2, 0.1 on &, lowering through 3. The model moves rise evenly across each step, so the lowering is spread over count 3 rather than coming at its end. Ends in the "promenade apart" stance (the lead's left foot 1.319 along the line of travel from where the crossed promenade's frame puts the origin), lead on his left. Provisional clearance/reach repair (2026-11-18), for the owner's subjective review: remove the own-feet exemption and the body-test exclusion. The original crossed entry, every landing from count 2 onward, exit pose, body facing, rise profile, foot order, 1 2 & 3 timing, 10 cm close and late closing weight transfer are preserved. The first step is smaller; the outward second-step arcs and small body displacement replace footprint clipping and excessive hip lowering. Dense linear/eased sampling gives positive own-foot clearance, zero leg shortfall, at most about 11 cm hip lowering and passing lateral balance diagnostics. The full mannequin leg-capsule proxy still overlaps briefly by up to about 2.5 cm during the initial crossed-stance release (reduced from the old approximately 7.8 cm worst overlap); the close and final step clear the capsules. This remaining leg-clearance limitation is documented rather than treated as full mesh clearance.
